title: Access & Identity V2 — the Truthful Access milestone: W-45 · W-46 · W-47 · W-49 · W-50 · W-51(IA-7) + tier C certification
supersedes: w45-w50-truthful-access-execution.json — same milestone, extended with W-50's commit, W-51's IA-7 half, and the eleven-fixture matrix. The superseded file is deleted rather than kept, because two records of one milestone is how a plan of record becomes ambiguous (OD-4 is already that problem once).
relation_to_prior_records: Extends w14-declared-route-capability-table.json. Nothing in this session touched promotion, migrations, or the shared environment, so findings A (the W-0…W-12 tranche is on staging), B (W-8 crossed a promotion-binding announcement gate) and C (migration apply state is unverifiable from a worker session) of post-merge-certification-reconciliation.json STAND UNCHANGED.

mission.record_covers_multiple_sessions: This file is EXTENDED per session rather than forked, for the reason given in `supersedes`. Session 1 ended at 45e6488ed. Session 2 (W-51/IA-8, W49-F1) ended at 65520202c. Session 3 (W14-F1, backing-route completeness) ended at 16302dff3. Session 4 (the declaration binding, and W-15 sizing) ended at 0c79ba6c6. Session 5 (the sizing's precision, and the first three W-15 declarations) ends at 8dd961b6a. Session 6 (the reasoned-none sweep, W-43, W-42, and the tier D environment repair) ends at 36a0504a0.

what_this_milestone_is: The mission's product milestone: /organization/access derives and displays authoritative state, and the authorization paths underlying those claims are enforced. Presentation reflects authorization; presentation does not create authorization.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-49 + W49-F2 — finished and committed, not restarted
shipped_this_session.state_found: Uncommitted and passing in the worktree at session start. A worktree carrying work that already passes is indistinguishable, to the next session, from work that was abandoned. It is now two commits.
shipped_this_session.substance: The surface gates on canManageUsersAndRoles at the route boundary before ?section= resolves; both live rendering routes gate identically, so the duplicate is not an unguarded bypass; /organization filters the Access domain card from the same declaration, so navigation cannot offer a door admission refuses.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-50 — no inert capability is presented as a control (IA-R8, T-6)
shipped_this_session.state_found: Uncommitted, complete, and passing (11 tests). Verified before commit rather than assumed.
shipped_this_session.measurement: 36 of the catalog's 57 keys are named by no product source on an executable line.
shipped_this_session.mechanism: unenforcedPermissionKeys.json holds the inert set; offerableLevelsForRow drops a column whose every key is inert; a row inert in both renders one statement instead of three radios. The Capability Summary keeps a granted-but-inert row and marks it 'Granted · not enforced'.
shipped_this_session.grain_is_the_column: documents.read is enforced and documents.write is not, so a row-level verdict would be wrong in both directions.
shipped_this_session.not_a_revocation: applyGridRowSelection runs only when a control changes, and an absent control cannot change. Asserted directly.
shipped_this_session.why_json_not_typescript: scanEnforcement walks .ts/.tsx under web/lib. As TypeScript literals these 36 keys would each acquire an enforcement site, emptying the derived set so the both-directions lock would pass by agreeing with nothing.
shipped_this_session.not_RL_35: RL-35's build-time form still waits on OD-3. IA-R8's presentation clause needs no decision: whether a row is a CONTROL is settled by whether anything enforces it, and that is knowable today.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-51 — IA-7, and the M2-17 composition the plan records but does not price
shipped_this_session.defect_display: user_roles is keyed on (user_id, org_id, role), so a membership is a SET. displayRoleForAdminPicker collapsed it and four places rendered the survivor as the whole answer: the roster row, the detail header, the Overview's Role field, and the search haystack — where a member holding {admin, regional_lead} was unfindable by 'regional lead'.
shipped_this_session.defect_counts: The Roles chapter counted members by the collapsed value and filtered its Users tab the same way, so a role that is never anyone's primary reported ZERO holders while the resolver was unioning its grants into live requests. Both now ask one predicate, so the count and the list cannot disagree.
shipped_this_session.defect_destructive: M2-17. The read collapses, the editor is seeded from the collapsed value, and PATCH /api/admin/users/[userId]/role replaces EVERY role row for the pair. Changing the one visible role of a principal holding {admin, regional_lead} deleted regional_lead, having never shown it. The one guard present made it worse: disabling the save while editRole === primary_role removed the harmless no-op and left only the submissions that reach the destructive path.
shipped_this_session.remedy: replacementIsNoOp asks the union, so a multi-role membership is correctly reported as a change; the loss is itemized by name; the save requires an explicit acknowledgement that resets on any change of principal or target; and the guard sits in front of the write in saveRole, not only on the button — a disabled attribute is a presentation fact, and this platform's rule is that presentation reflects authorization rather than creating it.
shipped_this_session.scope_limit_stated: This does NOT make the write additive. That is W-17, which needs an API that can add a role without removing the others. Until then the control says 'Replace with', because that is what it does. The card's claim that 'One role is supported per user today' described the picker, not the platform, and is gone.
shipped_this_session.why_not_deferred_to_W_17: The plan sequences IA-7 with W-17 because W-17 makes multi-role reachable. But multi-role memberships already exist — the plan's own census names one — so the display half is a present untruth and the destructive half is present data loss. Neither needs W-17 to be worth closing, and neither preempts its design.

shipped_this_session.workstream: Tier C — the eleven-fixture certification matrix
shipped_this_session.why_this_shape: The mission's acceptance form is that the UI, the route/API, and effective authorization AGREE — not that each behaves defensibly alone. Three passing per-layer suites can still describe a surface hidden in navigation and reachable by URL. Every fixture therefore derives all three answers and asserts the agreement itself, including as a set-cardinality check so a change that moves all four consumers together in the WRONG direction still has to move them together.
shipped_this_session.the_route_answer_is_the_route_s: requireUsersRolesManageAuth runs with its access-context dependency mocked at the module boundary. What is certified is the helper the Access routes actually call. That the mock is in effect is self-evidencing: the real resolver cannot return 200 without a database.
shipped_this_session.defect_found_in_own_work: The URL-reachability assertion was tautological on first writing — `reachable` and `offered` were the same expression, certifying nothing. Rewritten to compose the page's two refusals in the page's order from the exported predicates; that the page applies them in that order is proved separately by RL-36 against the real page source.
fixtures: capability permits but scope excludes the target
shipped_this_session.layer_separation_proved: F9 is admitted by capability and still bounded to one location; F1 holds the same capability bounded by nothing. The distinction is therefore real and not an artifact of every fixture being restricted.
shipped_this_session.negatives_asserted_directly: For every unset-profile fixture: scopeSummary must NOT return 'All locations', certainty is 'unset', the divergence reason is present, and allow-list rows are withheld. IA-3 as a test rather than a claim.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W14-F1 — the disclosure half, which was never the half that needed a decision
shipped_this_session.why_this_was_actionable: W-14 recorded the finding and declined to answer it because asserting that a roster read needs no capability is W-15's product call. That reasoning is correct and unchanged — and it was applied to the wrong half. The finding has two: WHO REACHES the route is a product question; WHAT IT DISCLOSES to whoever reaches it is not. Only the first needed an operator.
shipped_this_session.defect: GET /api/admin/users is admitted by portal eligibility alone and returned every org member's email address to everyone it admitted. The live consumer that made this matter is components/admin/opportunity/OperationalWorkAssigneeSelect.tsx, which needs to NAME a colleague in an assignee dropdown and derived that name from the local-part client-side — `label: row.email?.trim() || row.label` — so the full address crossed the wire in order to be rendered whole. Any staffer who could assign work could read the organisation's entire email list out of a <select>.
shipped_this_session.remedy: The label is computed at the route for every caller; the address is projected against canManageUsersAndRoles. No consumer loses a function — the picker shows the same names, the Access surface reads from the gated members route as before, and the legacy tables already handled email === null, which has always been in AdminUserRow's contract for an unreadable auth record.
shipped_this_session.admission_deliberately_unchanged: The declaration stays 'pending' rather than being quietly resolved, and its note is AMENDED rather than cleared. The gate is read from the bundle getAdminContextCached already resolved, so it costs no second auth pass — and it must NOT be re-derived from getAdminAccessContextCached, which does not require portalEligible and would widen who reaches the route while appearing to tighten it. Two tests assert that exact accident, one of them a caller who is portal-refused while holding the managing grant.
shipped_this_session.certification_shape: The agreement tests run the real handler and feed its real JSON to the real consumer's fetcher, then assert what the dropdown would put on screen. Three passing per-layer suites can still describe a route that withholds an address and a component that renders one from somewhere else.
shipped_this_session.non_vacuity: Proved by defeating the gate: the two disclosure assertions fail and the other thirteen do not.
shipped_this_session.still_open: The admission question. W14-F1 is NOT closed — its disclosure half is.

shipped_this_session.workstream: The backing-route record is discovered, not enumerated
shipped_this_session.defect_class: A sound check over an unsound subject. surfaceCapabilityDeclaration asserts that every route a chapter NAMES declares that chapter's capability, but backingRoutes is hand-authored — so a chapter calling a route nobody wrote down does not fail the join, it never enters it. This initiative has already been bitten by this shape (W-5, 'does the lock DISCOVER or ENUMERATE?').
shipped_this_session.measurement: The Users chapter issues six requests and declared three; the Roles chapter issues four and declared two. Six omissions.
shipped_this_session.why_nothing_was_broken: Every omitted route is correctly gated — users POST, users/[userId]/remove, rbac/roles, rbac/roles/[role_key], rbac/permissions and rbac/grants all declare settings.users_roles in W-14's table. Which is precisely why nothing said anything. A record that can only be audited by the person who wrote it is not a control.
shipped_this_session.remedy: The declaration is completed, and the new lock's subject is DISCOVERED from each chapter's own source, with dynamic segments normalised on both sides so `[userId]` and `${encodeURIComponent(id)}` compare as one path.
shipped_this_session.grain_decides_the_classification: capabilitiesDeclaredBy unions over a file's methods, and the divergence ratchet asserts a divergent route does NOT declare the capability. rbac/roles, rbac/grants and rbac/permissions read through requirePortalOrUsersRolesManageAuth, which admits portal-eligible principals lacking the grant — wider than the chapter's gate. They are still BACKING routes, because their files DO declare settings.users_roles; the wider read leg is recorded in W-14's table as W-13's portal.access question. Listing them as divergent would have failed the ratchet and stated something false.
shipped_this_session.non_vacuity: Removing rbac/permissions from the roles declaration makes the lock name that exact route and fail.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-15 prerequisite — the declared capability stops being a sentence in a JSON file
shipped_this_session.defect_class: A control that asserts rather than checks. As W-14 shipped it, {"status":"declared","capability":"settings.users_roles"} said nothing about the handler: deleting the guard it named left the check green. The mission's requirement is that the declaration BECOME enforcement.
shipped_this_session.why_this_had_to_precede_the_burndown: Driving 725 pending entries to `declared` against an unbound table would have produced 751 unfalsifiable claims instead of 25. The burndown's value is entirely contingent on the declaration meaning something.
shipped_this_session.three_joins: Each declared entry naming a helper must survive: (1) the exported handler's OWN body calls that helper — method grain, so a guard on GET cannot vouch for DELETE in the same file; (2) a verdict bound to an identifier is TESTED, because a returned verdict nobody branches on is not a gate; (3) the module defining the helper names the declared capability on an executable line.
shipped_this_session.not_the_retired_census: The census read source and INFERRED a gate, over-reporting enforcement by ~30×. This reads a stated claim and tries to FALSIFY it. Inference invents authorization nobody wrote; falsification can only remove a claim the table already makes.
shipped_this_session.finding_over_declaration: configuration/programs POST declared helper `canWriteProgramPublication` — a function that exists nowhere in the repository. The gate was real and correct throughout (POST has always called canManageProgramPublication, requiring settings.manage), but the table named an enforcement site a reviewer could not follow. Corrected, with the history kept in the note so it is not misread as a behaviour change.
shipped_this_session.finding_under_declaration: persons/[id]/profile-photo GET calls the very assertDocumentAccess that documents/[id]/signed-url declares as documents.read, while sitting `pending`. The table under-reports as well as over-reports. Its POST and DELETE stay off the worklist deliberately: they gate on `ctx.role !== "admin"`, a gate but not a capability gate, and which key replaces a raw role check is W-15's product call.
shipped_this_session.own_defects_caught_by_fixtures_not_inspe: Both would have convicted working code. Blanking string DELIMITERS as well as contents erased the token structure that tells an import from prose; and taking the first `{` after a handler name yields the destructured `{ params }` parameter rather than the body.
shipped_this_session.non_vacuity: Each join is proved to bite against a fixture built to fail exactly that one — including the shape table mutation cannot reach: a handler that calls the gate and discards the verdict, which reads as gated, greps as gated, and admits everyone. Fixtures live in a temp directory, never under app/api, so a run killed mid-test cannot leave a stray route in the app tree.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-15 sizing — the lane acquires a shape
shipped_this_session.why: 725 pending is a number, not a plan. Reading each pending handler's own body at method grain reports what gate evidence it carries, so the lane can be released by decision class rather than walked in directory order.
shipped_this_session.load_bearing_figure: 304 — the last three buckets. Handlers with no discovered authorization beyond authentication. That is W-15's risk concentration, and a far smaller thing to reason about than 725.
shipped_this_session.direction_of_error_is_the_whole_argument: The census's load-bearing output was 'this route is protected', which is unsafe when wrong because it retires scrutiny. This one's is 'no gate found here', which is conservative when wrong. A false alarm costs a reviewer five minutes; a false all-clear costs an exposure nobody looks for again. Nothing here feeds pass/fail.
corrections_from_disbelieving_the_first_: `none` first read 107, with analytics/placements in it while calling requireAnalyticsV2AdminContext. A first-party require/assert/ensure/can helper whose verdict the handler tests IS a gate — just not a capability gate. Converting those 276 is the actual substance of W-15, so they get their own bucket.

`capability` first read 80, on literals like `customer_id.is.null` and `person.email` — supabase filters and column paths that satisfy the key grammar and are not permission keys. That is C1's error at small scale. The grammar is now a prefilter and the catalog is the judge, taking the bucket to 2 — both already-known open items, which is the tool declining to invent a third.
shipped_this_session.duplicate_catalog_is_locked_not_trusted: Judging by catalog needs the catalog inside a .mjs that runs in prebuild, where the TypeScript discovery helper cannot be imported. Two independent catalog parsers that silently disagree is how the '35 keys' figure survived three workstreams, so the copy is asserted equal to the original.
shipped_this_session.scanner_now_reads_every_handler: Four handlers were unreadable. documents/entity-options nests a template literal inside another's interpolation, and a scanner taking the first backtick as the closing one loses brace balance for the rest of the file; three v2 drawer routes are pure `export { GET } from …` re-exports whose bodies live in their v1 counterparts. The tokenizer now carries a mode stack and re-exports are followed. Unreadable is 0 across all 751 handlers, and both fixes have fixtures — 'could not read' silently equalling 'fine' is the failure §10.2 already records.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-15 sizing — 'no gate found here' stops being mostly wrong, and the lane's first three declarations
shipped_this_session.why_this_and_not_the_burndown: Session 4 handed the operator a risk concentration of 304 handlers, 67 of them carrying no discovered authorization at all, and recommended asking for a POLICY per decision class. Before anyone is asked to rule on the size of a class, the class has to be measured correctly. Reading the 67 by hand, 37 were gated. A list that is more than half false alarms gets triaged like noise — which is the precise mechanism by which a check designed to be conservative stops being conservative. Session 4's direction-of-error argument is sound and it is not self-executing.
shipped_this_session.defect_class: Two shapes, four instances — an ENUMERATED answer where a discovered one was needed, and a body read against the WRONG FILE. Both are shapes this initiative has already paid for (W-5's locks, session 3's backing routes, §10.2's destructured parameter).

defects.delegation_read_as_absence: `jobs` exports a perf shell — `GET(request) { if (!adminPerfEnabled()) return getJobsImpl(request); … }` — and the impl carries both the context load and the scope resolution. Reading only the exported body reported one of the most heavily guarded routes in the tree as carrying no gate. Session 4 taught the reader to follow a re-export ACROSS files for this exact reason; this is the same defect one hop shorter. The hop is one hop, same file, and a fixture asserts a second local hop is NOT followed — an unbounded walk is the retired census's closure, and a stopping rule nobody tests is not a rule.
defects.enumerated_authority_vocabulary: The context-load signal was a hand-written regex of four names. `loadAdminRouteGate` resolves the access bundle and 403s a caller who is not portal-eligible, and matches none of them — so every route entering through the newer, preferred gate helper THIS INITIATIVE introduced read as ungated. An enumerated vocabulary makes the better code look worse, which inverts the signal it exists to produce. The roots stay small and auditable; the second layer is now DISCOVERED — a helper is an authority entry when its own declaration calls a root. Asked of the declaration rather than of the module, because a module that authenticates somewhere is not a module whose every export authenticates; crediting a route for calling a formatter that happens to live beside a gate is reachability standing in for enforcement.
defects.return_type_read_as_body: `async function f(): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; response: NextResponse }> { … }` opens two braces at paren depth zero before its body starts. `bodyBlock` took the first and returned a fragment of a type annotation — no calls, no gate — so a helper that authenticates in its first statement read as inert. This is §10.2's destructured-parameter defect one syntactic position later, and it stayed hidden because route handlers are typed `Promise<NextResponse>` and have no braces to trip on. It surfaced only when the same reader was pointed at LIBRARY helpers, whose inline union return types are ordinary. `loadConfigLayoutAssistAdminContext` is the case that found it: seven config-layout-assist handlers reported as carrying no authorization because of a brace in a signature.
defects.body_matched_against_the_wrong_file: The three v2 drawer routes are one line — `export { GET } from "@/app/api/admin/view-models/…"`. `handlerBody` correctly followed the re-export and returned a body containing `loadAdminRouteGate(…)`, which was then matched against the V2 file's import table. That table is empty. A body and an import table taken from two different files resolve nothing, and three gated routes were reported as carrying no authorization. Barrel re-exports are now followed for the same reason: six processing-identity handlers import `resolveOperatorRoute` from a directory barrel that declares nothing, and asking the barrel whether it authenticates gets 'no'. A barrel is a pass-through, not a hop — following one finds the first implementation rather than reading a second.

shipped_this_session.measurement: `none` falls 67 → 28. The composition matters more than the count: exactly ONE survivor is an `app/api/admin/*` route, against 19 before. The other 27 are token-bearing public routes, action links, webhooks and build metadata — the population the bucket should contain. Buckets at 8dd961b6a: capability 2, gateHelper 281, role 144, authenticated 267, none 28, unreadable 0 — reconciling to 722 pending.
shipped_this_session.the_one_admin_survivor: app/api/admin/work-units/[id]/provisioning-answer GET. Hand-verified GATED: `composeProvisioningAnswerForRoute` resolves the canonical route gate (its own header records U-P1, 'authorization + tenant scope resolved ONCE, by the canonical route gate') and returns a `gate` the handler refuses on. It remains flagged because reaching that gate is route → composer → loadAdminRouteGate → root, which is two hops, and the derivation is deliberately one.
shipped_this_session.what_was_NOT_done_and_why: The derivation was not made transitive. A fixed point over the authority relation would have cleared that last survivor and would have been defensible — each step requires a helper's own body to CALL the previous entry, which is not the census's 'something in the import closure mentions a primitive'. It was still declined, for two reasons. Every added hop weakens the property that an answer is checkable by opening two files; and every added hop shrinks the alarm set, so being wrong about it is wrong in the unsafe direction — the exact failure the bucket exists to avoid. Twelve admin survivors was a reviewable number, so they were reviewed by hand instead. Hand review is what the bucket is FOR.
shipped_this_session.no_lock_was_loosened: `bindDeclaration` still reads the exported handler's body and nothing else, so a DECLARED route that hides its guard behind a delegation still fails join 1 and must be rewritten or re-declared. Sharpening a measurement and loosening a lock are opposite moves and only one of them is safe here. The single change running the other way is a tightening: an authority verdict the handler never branches on is no longer counted as a gate — `const gate = await loadAdminRouteGate();` followed by a read of `gate.orgId` and no test of `.ok` establishes nothing — and such a handler now falls to `none` where a reviewer will see it. That is the rule the gate-helper bucket already applied, asked of the roots too.
shipped_this_session.declarations_recorded_not_imposed: Three, and all three change who may call the route by NOTHING — which is exactly what makes them Director-ownable where the rest of W-15 is not. persons/[id]/profile-photo GET already called the `assertDocumentAccess` that documents/[id]/signed-url declares as documents.read, and already refused on `decision.outcome !== 'allowed'` BEFORE the signed URL is minted; the table was under-reporting a route that enforces. Its POST and DELETE stay pending deliberately — they gate on `ctx.role !== 'admin'`, a gate but not a capability gate, and which key replaces a raw role check is W-15's product call. customer-person-role-types DELETE and person-relationship-type-settings DELETE are unconditional 405 stubs: no parameters, no request read, no client, NOT_IMPLEMENTED on every call. There is no action to authorize, which is precisely what `status: none` + reason exists to record.
shipped_this_session.ratchet: 725 → 722. Lowering the ceiling was forced by the ratchet's own non-vacuity check, which asserts that subtracting one from the ceiling produces a violation — an assertion that holds only while pending sits exactly at the ceiling. Slack in a ratchet is a ratchet that has stopped ratcheting.
shipped_this_session.draining_a_worklist_must_not_retire_the_: Declaring profile-photo emptied `pendingWithKnownGates`, and three tests that asserted it was non-empty began failing. Two could have been 'fixed' by asserting emptiness — but a discovery that has quietly stopped working also returns []. The live table is now asserted DRAINED, and the same discovery is run against a table with the declaration removed to prove it still finds the case. The third test — that the worklist does not claim profile-photo's mutations — was passing vacuously over an empty list, and now reads from the regressed table too. This is the tautology session 4 caught itself writing in the fixture matrix, in a second place.
shipped_this_session.non_vacuity: Eight fixtures, each built to fail exactly one defect. Two proved by REVERSION rather than by argument: disabling the return-type skip convicts the return-type fixture and nothing else; replacing the barrel walk with the module itself convicts the barrel fixture and nothing else. A ninth asserts the reader still refuses to call a genuinely ungated handler gated, because every other fixture in the block widens what is recognised.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-15 — the reasoned-`none` sweep, which needed no operator decision and was the only W-15 lane that did not
shipped_this_session.state_found: UNCOMMITTED IN THE WORKTREE at session start, ratchet already moved 722 -> 695. Session 3 recorded the hazard exactly: 'a worktree carrying work that already passes is indistinguishable, to the next session, from work that was abandoned.' It was therefore verified against source rather than adopted.
shipped_this_session.verification_not_adoption: A `status: none` is a security assertion, so the load-bearing claims were FALSIFIED rather than read. booking-config and field-definitions take the org from ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID and filter `.eq('org_id', orgId)` with `is_visible_in_public_booking`, so a caller cannot steer the read at another tenant. resend verifies via Svix and returns 503 unconfigured / 400 missing headers / 400 invalid signature. twilio resolves a per-binding token and 503s when none resolves, 403 on a bad signature. The public-forms GET and PATCH both call `verifySubmissionBelongsToPublicEmbed`, and the PATCH write is further pinned to `created_via_public_link_id` and `status='draft'` — the token SCOPES the record rather than merely admitting the caller, which is stronger than the entry claimed.
shipped_this_session.arithmetic: 695 pending + 30 none + 26 declared = 751 handlers. Pending sits EXACTLY at the ratchet, which is what keeps the ratchet's own non-vacuity check biting.
shipped_this_session.composition_is_the_point: The 27 are the population the `none` bucket is supposed to contain — action-link and path-token routes, public forms, tour booking, webhooks, build metadata. Session 5 had already driven the bucket to 28 with exactly one `app/api/admin/*` survivor, hand-verified gated. That survivor is still NOT declared.
shipped_this_session.restraint_recorded: `book` and `slots` on the tour-booking surface were deliberately left pending: they classified into other gate-evidence buckets and were never measured as ungated. Declaring a route the pass did not examine is the inference this table exists to refuse.
shipped_this_session.residual_risk_not_silently_closed: leads/gutters, marketing/demo-request and vendor-application are unauthenticated writes with no rate limit. Recorded in the entries as an abuse surface and explicitly NOT resolved: there is no principal to authorize, so it is a throttling concern and does not belong in a capability table.

shipped_this_session.workstream: W-43 — every resolver read error denies (I-30ᴬ, RL-23, GAP-3's read-error leg)
shipped_this_session.why_this_lane_at_all: Session 5 concluded the lane was 'out of preparation to do' and recommended W-15 released by OD-7 and nothing else. That was true of W-15 and NOT true of the milestone: §20 of the plan of record states plainly that `AD-12` gates `W-41` but NOTHING gates `W-42` or `W-43`, and §21 states that GAP-12 — the milestone's own `restrictions_and_inheritance` clause — closes only when W-24, W-43 and W-45/W-47 all land. W-45/W-47 were already done. W-43 was ungated milestone work sitting behind an OD-7 that does not bind it.
shipped_this_session.defect: `resolveAdminAccessCore` handled a failed read four different ways, and the one whose error was SILENTLY DROPPED had the maximal failure default. `user_access_profiles` never destructured `error` at all, so a transient failure was indistinguishable from 'no row' and resolved the widest possible way: both scopes `all`. That is the mission's own complaint — 'All locations · All departments' asserted without resolution — one layer BENEATH the UI that W-47 taught to stop asserting it. A truthful surface faithfully renders a lie handed up from the resolver.
shipped_this_session.why_it_ships_while_W_7_stays_pinned: The distinction that makes this executable. ABSENT_PROFILE_ENFORCEMENT must stay `legacy-all` until M1 is applied or the 2 known profile-less principals are locked out (L1). A read FAILURE is a different population: a transient fault, not a missing row. Denying it changes nothing for any healthy read, carries no lockout risk, and does not wait on the migration. This is precisely why I-30 is stated in terms of failure rather than absence.
shipped_this_session.derived_not_restated: The failed-read answer is `resolveScopeAnswerFromProfile(null, 'deny')`, so 'deny' cannot come to mean two different things. It is `restricted` PLUS explicitly empty allow-lists — never `restricted` alone, or a principal holding user_department_access rows grants itself what the failed read was meant to withhold.
shipped_this_session.evidence_channel_kept_clean: A read failure is logged on its own channel and deliberately NOT through logScopeDivergence. OD-7.title: W-15 conversion policy — may recording an existing gate as a capability CHANGE who may act?
OD-7.why_it_is_ready_now_and_was_not_before: Session 4 correctly declined to walk 725 handlers in directory order and asked for a policy instead. Session 5 makes that ask answerable: the classes are now measured rather than estimated. 281 handlers enter through a first-party gate helper that is not a capability gate; 144 compare a role or a permission-key array inline; 267 establish the caller and nothing more; 28 carry no discovered authorization, and all but one of those are public by design. The question is not 722 rulings. It is one rule applied to two classes.
OD-7.the_decision: For a handler that today gates on something OTHER than a capability — a role comparison, a portal-eligibility check, a bespoke require* helper — is the conversion required to preserve the current admission set exactly, or may it move to the capability that best expresses the intent even where that widens or narrows who may act?
OD-7.recommendation: Preserve exactly, by default; widen or narrow only per-route with a named decision. Every conversion that changes the admission set is a security change wearing a refactor's clothes, and this initiative already has two isolated instances of precisely that shape (W14-F1's admission half, W49-F1's password-reset control). A preserving conversion is mechanical, reviewable by the existing three joins, and Director-ownable end to end; a changing conversion is not, and should not be smuggled in behind a burndown metric.
alternatives: Preserve exactly (recommended) — the capability chosen must admit precisely today's callers. Consequence: the sweep is mechanical and can proceed without further operator input, but it BANKS existing over-permission rather than fixing it; a route that admits every portal-eligible principal keeps admitting them, now with a capability key naming that fact. The over-permission becomes visible and attributable instead of invisible, which is the point.

Best-expressed intent — pick the capability the route ought to require. Consequence: genuinely fixes over-permission, and cannot be executed without a per-route product judgement about who loses access; every one of those is a potential live lockout, and W-8 already shows what an unannounced narrowing costs.

Split by class — preserve for the 267 authenticated-only handlers, best-intent for the 144 inline role checks. Consequence: defensible, since a raw role comparison is the population most likely to be wrong; but it puts 144 product decisions on the critical path and the lane stalls behind them.
OD-7.consequence_of_not_deciding: The sweep does not start. The declarations are bound and the sizing is trustworthy, so nothing further is gained by more tooling — the next unit of work in this lane is a conversion, and every conversion needs this rule.
OD-7.exact_work_unblocked: The 267 authenticated-only handlers and the 281 gate-helper handlers become a mechanical burndown against the existing three joins under option 1 — the largest single block of remaining W-15 work, and the last structural item standing between the Truthful Access surface and enforcement that matches it. The 144 inline role checks and the reasoned-`none` sweep over the 27 public routes proceed under any option.
OD-7.not_blocking_everything: Independent of this decision: tier D browser certification (blocked separately and environmentally — see blockers.tier_D_environment), IA-8's duplicate-route deletion, IA-9's overview, and W-17's additive role write.
